apps.name: sitar guru
apps.pitch: pluck a string, reachy leans its head like a tuning needle and coaches you in french
apps.description:
an embodied sitar tuning coach. the robot's own mic (16 kHz, over WebRTC) feeds a YIN pitch tracker; the deviation in cents drives head roll continuously at ~10 Hz (±50 ¢ mapped to ±25° — the head *is* the needle), and a pregenerated french phrase book says « plus haut ! » / « plus bas ! » / « parfait ! ».

the cool details: YIN rather than an FFT peak, because the sitar's jawari bridge routinely makes a partial louder than the fundamental and a spectral picker locks onto the wrong harmonic. the DSP core (YIN, tuning tables, cents/swara maths) is ported verbatim from the web tuner in `BelCorentin/art`, so the two agree to the cent. the coach is a pure state machine — you hand it (now, track) and it hands back actions — so a whole six-string session is testable from a scripted pitch sequence with no clock, no audio and no robot. it also checks you are on the string it asked for (« ça, c'est le jod — on cherche le baj ») and gives in after three stubborn repeats. no TTS in the loop: the vocabulary is a finite function of the preset, so all 46 phrases are synthesised once at setup and cached as WAVs.
apps.status_detail: 48 offline tests green; whole session demo-able with --dry-run --source demo. never run against the live robot — README has a 'Still needs live-robot validation' checklist (does it hear its own voice? does the roll sign read backwards?).

apps.name: mémoire
apps.pitch: alzheimer memory companion — french care profile, journal, and a phone page for the family
apps.description:
a memory companion aimed at people with alzheimer's / memory troubles, built *on top of* pollen's `reachy_mini_conversation_app` (a dependency, not a fork): a french care profile — calm, short sentences, never quizzes, gently reorients — plus SQLite journal tools plugged in through the app's external profile/tool mechanism.

`journal_event` silently logs notable moments (visits, meals, medication, mood); `recall_journal` answers « qu'est-ce que j'ai fait aujourd'hui ? ». a second FastAPI server runs in-process on :7870, token-authenticated: /famille is a senior-friendly remote for the family (three huge buttons — play a recorded voice message on the robot speaker, take a camera snapshot, or have a written message spoken verbatim via edge-tts), /care is the caregiver dashboard whose honest signal is *repeated questions over 30 days with a week-over-week trend*, clustered from the person's own words, no model opinions.

face seeking (needs daemon ≥ 1.9.0): when nobody has been in frame for ~8 s the body sweeps in widening yaw legs (±60° → ±120° → ±150°) until the tracker finds a face, then anchors — the robot turns around to look for people instead of staring at a wall.

this one is also the house style for the launchpad you're reading: FastAPI + everything inline, no CDN, works on a LAN with no internet.
apps.status_detail: bring-up verified 17-08-2026 (connection, bidirectional WebRTC audio, camera, profile + journal tools, realtime session + french greeting). face lock verified live 19-08-2026 (sweep found a face at 120°). still pending: a full conversation-level session and the tailscale funnel path.
notes: needs HF auth (`hf auth login` or HF_TOKEN) — inference is hugging face's cloud realtime backend.
desk dev without the robot: start `reachy-mini-daemon --sim` (MuJoCo) first, then ./run.sh --ui. no dev button here because that daemon is a separate process the launchpad does not own.
NEVER tunnel :7860 — the upstream UI has no auth. only :7870 (token-authed) may be exposed, via scripts/expose.sh.
'command accepted' ≠ 'robot moved' — the only ground truth is reading encoders back (/api/state/present_head_pose).
after a daemon self-update the robot can be wedged (commands accepted, nothing moves): POST /api/daemon/restart then re-enable motors.

apps.name: jukebox
apps.pitch: show a hand sign, reachy plays that song — and dances to it, body on the bass, head on the melody
apps.description:
camera frame → mediapipe's stock GestureRecognizer (pretrained, zero training) → debounce (N consecutive frames + cooldown + release-before-refire) → the song streams to the robot speaker. 👍 upbeat, 👎 beethoven, ✌️ libertango, ✊ stop, ☝️/👇 volume (hold to keep stepping).

music is *streamed* over the WebRTC audio channel at 16 kHz ~0.4 s ahead of real time rather than uploaded as a file — that's what makes live gain changes possible mid-song, starts playback instantly, and gives the dance a sample-exact clock.

the dance is the nice part: each song is analysed once in pure numpy — BPM by onset autocorrelation plus three 20 Hz envelopes (broadband, low 40–250 Hz, high 1–4 kHz) cached as a .dance.json sidecar. the BODY follows the low band (tango-like yaw circle, z pulse on the beat), the HEAD follows the high band (pitch nods on the beat, roll wiggle at double time, accented on melodic transients) — so the accordion runs visibly ride on top of the body motion, decorrelated from it. libertango gets both layers doing different things; that's the whole point.
apps.status_detail: 19 offline checks green, gesture path exercised on the laptop webcam. on-robot playback + dance not yet live-tested (vault status 19-08-2026: « next: test jukebox robot allumé »).

apps.name: narrator
apps.pitch: reachy watches the room and narrates what changes, in french, out loud in your terminal
apps.description:
a camera frame every N seconds goes to claude (sonnet, vision) and comes back as a one-line french narration. the trick is that the model keeps context between frames, so it narrates *changes and events* — « quelqu'un entre », « il s'assoit » — instead of re-dumping the same static scene forever; when nothing changed it answers RAS, logged and printed as a dim heartbeat.

context strategy: only the *current* frame is ever sent as an image. after each call the image turn is replaced by a text placeholder `[image à <ts>]` and the window is trimmed to the last 10 exchanges — so context stays cheap and text-only while the model still remembers what it already said. everything lands in logs/narration-<date>.jsonl, and `--recap` summarises the day in a single call.

built for a memory-impaired household: concise, factual, no chatter.

apps.name: reachying for the stars
apps.pitch: show a ✌️ and reachy unlocks the next fact from your curiosity vault, spoken on its own speaker
apps.description:
the first app, and the odd one out: a reachy mini *JS* app that runs in the browser on the host shell (mountHost / connectToHost, SDK npm 1.8.0) and is deployed as a hugging face Space — nothing to launch from this laptop, you open it.

facts are a build-time snapshot exported from the obsidian curiosity vault by scripts/export_facts.py, which also pregenerates the speech (edge-tts → 16 kHz mono PCM WAV) so the fact plays on the *robot's* speaker with daemon-side motion/audio sync via playMove — one clock for audio and the talking gesture, instead of the browser's speechSynthesis and a robot bobbing along blind.

sign detection is mediapipe tasks-vision running in-browser on the robot's WebRTC camera stream, model bundled locally.
apps.status_detail: shipped 27-07-2026 as the private HF Space `ilikeitlikeit/reachying-for-the-stars` and opened from the robot's app store. not re-verified since the daemon went to 1.9.0.
